"I-I wanted to go meet you at the train, I really did, but-but Master Chen insisted he'd go."

"Little Eight wasn't going to fight the Squire over it, so I just did chores and waited. That's all I did, just waited."

Hua Jiunan stroked the little serpent's head, his voice gentle. "I know, Eighth Master. It's all right."

As they spoke, the Shameless Cocoon and Grand Warden Xin Lianshan came through the gate flanking Radiant Lady Guanghua and Snow Corpse, one on each side like ceremonial guards.

The warden had finally gotten his wish — a transfer to the Radiant Lady's mansion as the Divine Commander of the Imperial Guard. In the old reckoning that was a proper second-rank official, the kind of post an emperor gave only to his most trusted favorite. Xin Lianshan these days was insufferably pleased with himself.

Spotting Hua Jiunan and Chen Daji, he murmured a request to Snow Corpse, then came wiggling over, big rear end swaying, at the fastest waddle he could manage.

"Hahaha, Little Master, Young General — you're home!"

"Old Xin missed you somethin' fierce!"

"Old Xin's doing just fine, don't you worry about me none!"

The menace grimaced. "Who's worrying about y—"

He never finished. Firecrackers went off in every direction, and everyone froze — then burst out laughing, all together, shouting: "IT'S NEW YEAR!"

And in the middle of the nation's great celebration, Wang San, little Qianyue, and the Fox Maiden came out supporting Deaf Granny and Uncle Li on either arm. Behind them, shy as ever, walked Little Wuxin.

"Namu Amitabha, big brother!"

**EXTRA: So Many Injustices in This World**

Time galloped, and twenty years went by in a blink. Hua Jiunan was forty now.

Because he had spent his own life to bring Wuxin back, his temples had gone white long ago. But the white hair didn't age him — if anything it gave him the particular charm of a mature man. In the parlance of young women these days: a dad-type. A dad-type overflowing with the hard-won security of the years.

Compared to him, that Chen fellow had changed hardly at all. Age had left a few marks on his face, but not one mark on his character.

It was one in the morning when the wretch tiptoed into Chang Baye's room.

The great serpent — honest, hardworking, dreaming only of earning an honest living for his wife and kids — had spent the whole day planting herbs in the fields and was dead asleep.

That Chen fellow leaned in, wicked as sin, and SCREAMED in his ear.

"Who's there?! What happened?!"

"Why'd you scream so awful?!"

"ASSASSINS!"

The word assassin settled it. Without a moment's hesitation he launched himself like a bottle rocket, shot out the window, and streaked straight for Hua Jiunan's room. In the good serpent's heart, his Little Master is always the first thought.

Never mind that the Master was middle-aged now. Never mind that the Master had long since been unbeatable in all three realms.

Yet at Hua Jiunan's door, Chang Baye stopped short.

No sound from inside. That meant the Master was still sleeping.

If the Master was sleeping, there were no assassins. The serpent held it as absolute doctrine that nothing in heaven, earth, or underworld could take Hua Jiunan by surprise — not even the Three Ancestors of the Human Race themselves.

"Master's fine. That's what matters," the great serpent whispered, as quietly as his enormous body allowed. Then he paused.

"You scared? Scared, Daddy will come with you."

"You bring paper? Bring the soft kind, remember."

"You're too tender down there — the hard stuff'll chafe you."

"Little Jie?! What's wrong? Did Daddy do something wrong?"

"Or are you not feeling well?"

Chang Jie knew how deeply his father loved him, and for once answered at speed — instead of his usual glacial pace that could make a saint tear his hair out.

"Daddy, don't worry. It's a small problem."

"I had to poop, then I forgot, then you held me up — and I went in the shell."
